Here are the 14 points:

1. Open covenants of peace, openly arrived at, after which full freedom of agreement shall be secured to all peoples.

7. Equal access to trade markets and the raw materials of nature without discriminatory treatment.
8. Adequate representation in governments to the peoples whose interests are affected by territorial changes.
9. Inclusion in the reorganization of all territories now under alien rule.
10. Adjusting the boundaries of all areas so small that they cannot defend themselves.
11. Restriction of arms until general disarmament has been carried out to satisfactory levels.
12. Adjustment of colonial claims of all peoples by fair and equal procedures.
13. Elimination from the customs relations of all territory now occupied by foreign powers.
14. A universal association of nations for mutual trust and confidence.

Wilson presented these points as part of his Fourteen Point Plan, which he hoped would guide the peace process and lead to lasting peace in Europe. While most of Wilson's specific proposals were not implemented, many elements of his vision have since shaped international relations and diplomacy, influencing subsequent treaties such as the Treaty of Versailles and the League of Nations.
